title: Read aloud so a listener can follow
description: Read a short text aloud so a listener can say what it was about.
oneStarDescription: Read a paragraph at a pace a listener can follow, without skipping a line.
twoStarDescription: Pause at a sentence end and stress the word that carries the point.
threeStarDescription: Ask the listener what the paragraph decided, and reread the sentence they missed.

title: Recite a short text from memory
description: Learn a short text and recite it, then repair the line you miss.
oneStarDescription: Recite a short stanza or paragraph without the page.
twoStarDescription: If you stop, take only the first word as a prompt and finish the line yourself.
threeStarDescription: Recite the whole text to a person, mark the line you missed, and say how you will practice that line.

title: Recognize a suspicious message
description: Spot signs that a message is trying to rush you into clicking or paying, and stop.
oneStarDescription: In a sample message, point to the ask and to one sign of pressure or a strange sender.
twoStarDescription: Say how you would reach the organization by an address you already know, without using the link in the message.
threeStarDescription: Say whether you would open it, delete it, or ask someone, and the reason.

title: Record a voice someone can understand
description: Record speech that a listener can understand on ordinary headphones.
oneStarDescription: Record a sentence in a quiet place and play it back.
twoStarDescription: If noise or distance gets in the way, move the microphone or the room and record again.
threeStarDescription: Play it to someone who was not there and ask them to repeat the sentence.

title: Remember a list along a route
description: Place a short list of items along a route you know, and recall them in order.
oneStarDescription: Choose a route you can picture and place each item of a short list at one spot.
twoStarDescription: Walk the route in your mind and say the items in order without looking.
threeStarDescription: Check against the list, name the item you missed, and change the picture you used for it.

title: Repot a plant
description: Move a plant into a slightly larger pot without burying the stem deeper than it was.
oneStarDescription: Slide the plant out and show whether the roots circle the ball.
twoStarDescription: Place it in the new pot at the same stem depth and fill around it.
threeStarDescription: Water it in, put it where it was growing, and name one sign that would make you ask for advice.

title: Return an item you bought
description: Return or start a return for an item, with the reason and the proof the seller asks for.
oneStarDescription: Find the seller's return rule and the date you bought the item.
twoStarDescription: Ask for the return in the seller's channel, with the reason and the proof they list.
threeStarDescription: Write what the seller said would happen next, or that they refused, and the date.

title: Review a week and change one thing
description: Look back at a week and change one plan because of what actually happened.
oneStarDescription: Write three things that happened and one that did not.
twoStarDescription: For the thing that did not happen, write one cause you can do something about.
threeStarDescription: Change one item in next week's plan because of that cause.

title: Review privacy settings you can see
description: Look at the privacy settings an account shows you and change one you understand.
oneStarDescription: Open the privacy or sharing page of an account you control and name one setting.
twoStarDescription: Change one setting and say what other people can no longer see, in the words the page uses.
threeStarDescription: Point to a setting you will not change because you do not know what it does.

title: Roast a tray of vegetables
description: Roast mixed vegetables so they brown instead of steaming in a crowded pan.
oneStarDescription: Cut vegetables to a similar size, roast them, and show a piece with color on the surface.
twoStarDescription: Point to a pale piece and say whether the tray was too full, then roast or rearrange so more surface can brown.
threeStarDescription: Roast two vegetables that cook at different speeds and take the faster one out, or cut it so both finish together.

title: Run a short meeting from an agenda
description: Lead a short conversation from an agenda and leave a note of what was decided.
oneStarDescription: Write three items and share them before the conversation.
twoStarDescription: During the conversation, park one off-topic point and return to the list.
threeStarDescription: Write what was decided and who does the next action, and check it with one other person.

title: Run a simple home observation
description: Change one ordinary thing, watch what happens, and write the result without a grand claim.
oneStarDescription: Write what you will change and what you will watch, before you start.
twoStarDescription: Make the change, write what you saw, and keep a note of what you did not see.
threeStarDescription: Write one sentence you will not claim, because you changed only one thing once.

title: Save and label a seed
description: Save a seed from food or a plant you grew, and label what it is and when you took it.
oneStarDescription: Take seeds from one plant or fruit and dry them so they are not damp to the touch.
twoStarDescription: Write the name and the date on the container.
threeStarDescription: Write whether you know if the seed will grow true, or that you do not know.

title: Say what could stop a plan
description: Name a way a small plan could fail, and change one step because of it.
oneStarDescription: Write a small plan in three steps.
twoStarDescription: Write one likely way it fails, based on a fact you can point to.
threeStarDescription: Change one step to reduce that failure, and say what you did not try to prevent.

title: Scale a recipe
description: Change a recipe for a different number of eaters and check one quantity by measuring.
oneStarDescription: Point to the yield of a recipe and the amount of one ingredient.
twoStarDescription: Rewrite that ingredient for a different number of people and measure it.
threeStarDescription: Name one step, such as pan size or time, that you would not multiply in the same way, and say why.

title: Season food by tasting
description: Taste food and add salt or acid until the flavor is balanced, without salting from habit.
oneStarDescription: Taste a dish before seasoning and say what is missing, using words such as flat or harsh.
twoStarDescription: Add a small amount of salt or a sour ingredient, taste again, and say what changed.
threeStarDescription: Season a dish for someone else and stop while you can still name one thing you chose not to add.

title: Send a package
description: Pack an object and hand it to a counter with the address and the service you chose.
oneStarDescription: Pack an object so it does not rattle, and close the box.
twoStarDescription: At home or at the counter, choose a service and say what the receipt says about delivery.
threeStarDescription: Keep the receipt or tracking number, and say where you stored it.

title: Set a table for a meal
description: Set a table so each person has what the meal requires.
oneStarDescription: Set a place with a plate, a glass, and the tool the meal needs.
twoStarDescription: Set every place the same way, with a clear path to sit.
threeStarDescription: Add or remove a tool because of the menu, and say why.

title: Set up a safe playing space
description: Set up a space for a game so the boundaries and the hazards are clear.
oneStarDescription: Mark the playing area and a place for bags and water.
twoStarDescription: Move one object that people could trip on, or move the game away from it.
threeStarDescription: Tell the group the boundary and what happens if a ball leaves it.

title: Sew a button back on
description: Sew a button so it stays closed through a buttonhole and the thread is finished.
oneStarDescription: Sew a button onto scrap or a garment and fasten the thread so it does not pull out.
twoStarDescription: Button it through the hole and show that the cloth is not pinched flat under the button.
threeStarDescription: Replace a missing button in line with the others, and say what you checked.

title: Shop from a meal plan
description: Buy what a meal plan needs and come home able to say what you skipped.
oneStarDescription: Turn a meal plan into a shopping list grouped so you can walk the shop once.
twoStarDescription: Buy the listed items or write a substitute next to anything you did not find.
threeStarDescription: Show one substitute and say which meal still works because of it.

title: Skim a text for your question
description: Search a chapter for the answer to a question you wrote first.
oneStarDescription: Write the question before you start reading.
twoStarDescription: Find a heading or a paragraph that bears on the question, and mark it.
threeStarDescription: Answer the question from that passage, or write that the chapter does not answer it.

title: Smooth a small piece of wood
description: Sand a small wooden offcut until the surface you chose is smoother than when you started.
oneStarDescription: Sand one face and show the difference with a fingertip or a side-by-side look.
twoStarDescription: Use a finer grit after a coarser one, and say which scratch the finer grit is removing.
threeStarDescription: Stop before any oil or varnish, and say what you would need to know before adding one.

title: Solve a cube and explain one step
description: Solve a 3x3 cube with a method you can explain, not by speed.
oneStarDescription: Complete one stage of a written method, such as a cross or a first layer, and show it.
twoStarDescription: Perform one sequence and say what it is for, in ordinary words.
threeStarDescription: Solve the cube, and if you slip, return to the last stage you can recognize rather than starting in a panic.

title: Solve a logic grid
description: Solve a logic grid by marking what is impossible, not by guessing.
oneStarDescription: Read one clue and mark the cells it makes true or false.
twoStarDescription: Use a mark you already made to cross out another cell, and say which mark allowed it.
threeStarDescription: Fill the answer only where every alternative is crossed out, and test it against each clue.

title: Sort a wash before you start
description: Sort dirty clothes into loads the labels allow, before any machine starts.
oneStarDescription: Separate clothes into at least two piles using color or the care label.
twoStarDescription: Remove one item that does not belong, and say which symbol or risk made you do it.
threeStarDescription: Choose which pile to wash first and why, such as what you need tomorrow.

title: Split a shared cost
description: Split a shared bill in a way the group can check.
oneStarDescription: Write who owes what for a shared cost, including a tip or a tax if there is one.
twoStarDescription: Show that the shares add back to the total.
threeStarDescription: Change one person's share for a reason the group can see, and show the new sum.

title: Split work into next actions
description: Turn a vague task into the next visible action a person could do.
oneStarDescription: Write what finished looks like for one personal project.
twoStarDescription: Write the next action so someone else could tell when it is complete.
threeStarDescription: Write three actions in the order they must happen, and mark the one that is blocked.

title: Spot a contradiction in your notes
description: Find two notes that disagree and decide which one you will check.
oneStarDescription: Point to two of your notes that cannot both be true.
twoStarDescription: Write which source or page you will open to settle it.
threeStarDescription: After checking, strike or rewrite the note that was wrong, and leave the date of the correction.

title: Squat with control
description: Squat down and stand up with a stable foot position, and stop if pain is sharp.
oneStarDescription: Squat to a depth you can stand up from, with both feet staying quiet on the floor.
twoStarDescription: Ask a person or use a side-on recording to name one fault, such as heels lifting, and repeat with that fault reduced.
threeStarDescription: Do a few repetitions and stop when form breaks or when you feel sharp pain, and say which stop you used.

title: Label a leftover
description: Put a leftover in a container with a name and a date, and say you are not deciding a medical storage rule.
oneStarDescription: Put leftover food in a clean container and close it.
twoStarDescription: Write what it is and the date you packed it.
threeStarDescription: Later, read the label and either use it if it still looks and smells as it did, or discard it if you are unsure.

title: Stretch and stop before pain
description: Stretch a muscle you can name and stop at strong tension rather than pain.
oneStarDescription: Move into a stretch for a muscle you can name, and point to where you feel it.
twoStarDescription: Hold only while the feeling is tension, and come out when it becomes pain or when you cannot breathe easily.
threeStarDescription: Stretch the other side and say which side felt tighter, without forcing them to match.

title: Summarize what someone said
description: Restate what someone said so they can correct you.
oneStarDescription: After someone speaks, say the main point in your own words.
twoStarDescription: Ask whether you missed something, and change your summary if they say you did.
threeStarDescription: In the summary, separate what they said happened from what they want to happen next.

title: Support a climbing plant
description: Give a climbing plant a support and tie it so the stem is held, not cut.
oneStarDescription: Put a stake or a string in place before the stem bends.
twoStarDescription: Tie the stem with a loop that does not pinch, and show a finger of room.
threeStarDescription: Look again after the plant has grown and move or loosen a tie that has become tight.

title: Take a photo with a clear subject
description: Take a photo in which a viewer can tell what the subject is.
oneStarDescription: Take a photo and say what the subject is before you show it.
twoStarDescription: Move yourself or the subject so the background does not compete, and show the new frame.
threeStarDescription: Name one fault in the first photo, retake it, and show that the fault is smaller.

title: Take a phone message
description: Take a message for someone else with the name, the ask, and the callback.
oneStarDescription: Write who called and what they want.
twoStarDescription: Read the number or the reply path back to the caller.
threeStarDescription: Give the message to the right person and say how urgent the caller said it was.

title: Teach a concept back
description: Explain a concept to someone and find the part you cannot yet say.
oneStarDescription: Explain one concept without reading, using an example.
twoStarDescription: Answer one question, or say you do not know, and mark that spot.
threeStarDescription: Check the spot you missed and explain that part again in one clearer sentence.

title: Tell a short true story
description: Tell a true story with a start, a change, and an end a listener can retell.
oneStarDescription: Tell a true event that includes what changed from the beginning to the end.
twoStarDescription: Tell it again in fewer sentences and ask the listener what they still understood.
threeStarDescription: Say one true part you did not tell, and why you left it out.

title: Tie a knot that holds and unties
description: Tie a knot that holds a load you can test, and untie it afterwards.
oneStarDescription: Tie a knot you can name around a rail or a ring, and tighten it so it sits flat.
twoStarDescription: Pull with a force you can stop, show that the knot stays, and then untie it.
threeStarDescription: Tie one firm knot and one slipped knot. Pull the free end of the slipped knot and show it opens, then say which knot you would use when the loop must come undone.

title: Tie a necktie or a scarf
description: Tie a necktie or a scarf so it stays and sits in the center.
oneStarDescription: Tie a standard knot from a diagram you can show, and tighten it gently.
twoStarDescription: Center the knot and set the ends to the length you intended. If it is a scarf, turn your head both ways and retie once if it slips.
threeStarDescription: Untie it and show that the cloth is not crumpled into a hard knot.
